members.note: The pool, in pool order, with RowSourceIndices saying what each one currently shows. GetRealizedRowCount / GetRowWidget are the questions a caller usually means.
True only for a drag of THIS list's own row -- a drag from elsewhere hovering over it is not this list dragging.
Throws the rows away and builds them again from the source, which is what UMG's does.
Forwarded to the scroll behaviour.
A list's notch is a ROW, so the multiplier scales the row pitch; the scroll box scales local units. Same name, same meaning, different unit underneath.
Capital B, which is this library's spelling everywhere. Takes EDreamScrollBoxScrollbarVisibility rather than ESlateVisibility.
See SetScrollbarVisibility.
Lower-case s in Overscroll, which is how the rest of this library spells it.
Signed local units past an end; zero in range and zero while overscroll is off.

UUIScrollView::bIsPointerScrollingEnabled, asked at the FRONT of AcceptsDragGesture and beside ConsumeMouseWheel::Never on the wheel road: the wheel and the drag are one gesture set, and a view that answers one but not the other is one whose scroll bar is the only way down.
Same switch, spelled the way the scroll box spells it so the two controls read alike.

UUIScrollView::bIsGamepadScrollingEnabled, asked by FDreamUINavigationScroll BEFORE AnalogMouseWheelKey. Refusing there means the gesture goes to nobody: an outer container is not a fallback for a switch the author turned off on the inner one.

Through the drag-drop subsystem, not by clearing our own flags: the operation, the visual and the pointer's state are ITS, and a list that only forgot its half would leave a visual on screen with nothing to end it. When the subsystem has nothing to cancel -- a headless test, a pointer already gone -- the control still clears its own state, or every later drag would look like one already in flight.

This control rebuilds synchronously, so there is no pending request to make: every setter that moves the source rebuilds before it returns, which is what a headless test and the designer's first frame both need.
Fires on every BIND, which while recycling is every time a row comes round to a new item.
Broadcast before RebuildRows returns, which IS the batch boundary here: this control rebuilds synchronously, so there is no pending request for a later frame to complete.
One instance per POOL row, filling the row; the row's face, height, hover and selection stay the control's. Null is the built-in label row.
Off by default: every existing list's reveal lands in one frame. Pushed to the behaviour's animated-wheel switch.
A SPEED on the list, a DURATION on the behaviour -- the same ease parameterised twice. Converted once, at the push, as a reciprocal.

New UUIScrollView::bAnimateTouchScrolling: at drag end the fling's projected landing is handed to the same glide the wheel uses, and the velocity dropped so the physics does not keep pushing what the tween is already moving.
Pushed to UUIScrollView::bAllowRightClickDragScrolling, which is the scroll box's spelling of the same switch.
See SetIsPointerScrollingEnabled.
See SetIsGamepadScrollingEnabled.

A branch in ScrollItemIntoView's target: the row is PINNED at a share of the window instead of merely brought inside it. What a cursor-driven menu wants -- the highlighted row stays put and the list moves under it.
0 is the near edge, 1 the far one, half the middle. Still clamped at both ends of the range, because the ends have no line to spare.

Off, and off is LITERAL: with it false no row carries a drag behaviour at all, so an existing list gains nothing to subscribe to and nothing that could change what a press on a row means. Turning it on adds UDreamListRowDragSource -- a subclass of the library's own UDreamUIDragSource, so the press-and-move test, the operation hand-off and the end-of-drag notification are the ones every other draggable widget uses.
Separate from bAllowDragging, and both directions are useful: a palette dragged OUT of but never into wants dragging alone, an equipment list taking items from elsewhere wants dropping alone.

Folded INTO the operation's single DragVisualOffset at drag time, because a pivot is an offset measured in the visual's own size and the library's operation carries one number for both. Needs the row's size, which is why it happens when there is a row rather than on the behaviour.
Added on top of the pivot, in local units. X right, Y up.
Null falls back to RowTemplateClass, which is the answer that needs no authoring: the thing under the cursor should look like the row it came from, and the list already knows how to make one.
UDreamDragDropOperation by default, which already carries a payload, a tag, a visual class and the cancel notification that outlives a recycled row.
A CLASS, not an instance: a list makes one visual per drag and a shared instance would be one widget two simultaneous drags fought over. The instance, once made, is the operation's.

Private state with a pure getter rather than a writable flag: it is set by the drag beginning and cleared by it ending, and a caller writing it would be lying to every handler that reads it. GetDraggedItemIndex answers which row.

True, on both roads: a navigation press that steps to another row selects it, as SListView's NavigationSelect does, and NavigateToIndex selects what it reveals. Off, both only move focus and reveal, and the selection stays where the player left it -- a list you scroll through without losing the line you were on.

A parked index set beside the live one: ReconcileSelection re-applies a parked index the moment the source is long enough to hold it, instead of dropping it. A screen restoring 'row 7 was selected' before its data loads would otherwise lose it silently. Turning the switch off discards the parked set.
Fired before the new index is written, so a handler asking GetRowItemIndex is still told the one being released.

A designer-time-only row count. This control builds its rows from the authored Items with no world and no layout pass, so the designer already sees the real list -- there is nothing for a preview count to stand in for.
